Through the quarter ended June 30, 2026 · weekly marks through the week ending October 11, 2026

The business

Uber runs a marketplace app. Riders pay for trips, people order food and groceries, and shippers book trucks. Drivers, couriers and carriers do the work and keep most of what the customer pays. Uber's revenue is its cut of that spend, plus a few lines it books in full.

That cut comes from three segments. Mobility (rides) is the engine and the profit centre. Delivery is the second leg and has been growing faster lately. Freight is a small, cyclical brokerage that has shrunk since 2022. Operating income turned positive in 2023, and free cash flow has climbed every year since 2021. Net income jumps around because Uber marks its stakes in other companies to market each quarter.

Risks

  • Durability break: drivers and couriers reclassified as employees, or a price war in rides. Watch Mobility revenue growth, operating income, and free cash flow.
  • Big swings in net income and EPS from investment marks can hide the operating trend.
  • Robotaxi players could own the rider relationship in dense cities.
  • Freight stays a drag tied to the trucking cycle.

Close competitors

  • Lyft — the U.S. rides rival.
  • DoorDash — the delivery leader in the U.S.
  • Grab — rides and delivery across Southeast Asia, the market Uber sold to it.
  • Waymo — driverless rides, now a partner in some cities and a rival in others.
